title: Cold rebuild: Build an email
summary: Rebuild Build an email from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Build an email** in *Builder*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

code: public Sentence Word(string w) { _words.Add(w); return this; }
public Sentence End(string e) { _end = e; return this; }

steps.title: Rebuild Build an email cold
prompt: Write `record Email(string[] To, string Subject, string Body)` and `class EmailBuilder` with:
- fluent `To(string address)` (can be called several times), `Subject(string s)`, `Body(string b)`
- `Email Build()` that throws `InvalidOperationException` if there is no recipient or no subject; the body defaults to `""`
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
record Email(string[] To, string Subject, string Body);
